title: metro: last light redux
text: One of the greatest games i have ever played. Great storyline, great atmosphere, amazing graphics, immersive world and characters.  This game has everything you would want in a single player experience and presents it in a way that is immersive, suspenseful, and uniquely satisfying.   The world of the Metro is beautifully brought to life, yet retains a darkness and grit to it that i have yet to see in any other game.  I dont usually like "suspense" or "horror" games, but this game changed my mind. Both metro games have elements of stealth, heartpounding horror around every corner, intense gunfights, mysterious and dastardly enemies, deep characters background, all wrapped up superbly in a terrifying world filled with monsters and men alike, in a believable atmosphere that delivers an elegant depiction of the good, bad and the ugly of humanity.  Moral choices will affect your game experience and the thought provoking storyline with leave you wanting to come back for more.  I can honestly say i was sad when i finished it.  I would recommend this game to anyone regardless of your particular taste in videogames.  A MUST PLAY!

title: metro: last light redux
text: Last Light is a great sequel to 2033 that very subtly improves upon aspects of the first game and also treads some new ground. By that, I mean it's not immediately apparent in the beginning, where it feels like "more of the same" but as the game progresses, the improvements and differences slowly surface. The atmosphere is still great, if ever so slightly more fleshed out and this is aided by a bigger variety of locations in the aptly named Venice, the quirky and colorful Theatre and the eerie Dead City. Ofcourse, this is in addition to the familiar endless tunnels, the cobweb ridden catacombs, the barren surface (which is a lot less whiter this time around) and the usual grim goodness that we love. The level design (which I found a little weak in the first game) is slightly better with less awkward enemy positions and better, smoother opportunities to stealth your way through. Gunplay is pretty much the same, with only two new snipers bring added. However, I did feel like the combat AI is a little too aggressive even on normal difficulty, but one could see it as an extra challenge. Coming to the mutants, the Nosalises and Watchmen are still super jumpy, the Demons are unpredictable and the new additions, the swamp inhabitant Shrimp family probably takes the cake for the most annoying. But there is a bigger spread between scripted encounters and the ones resulting from exploration. The counterpart for the Librarian encounter from the first game isn't quite as epic or heart pounding, but it does serve a different purpose (spoiler). The horror factor is upped a little bit, but it's still a survival game first. The story is done well too. Artyom feels more a like a character than just the mute guy you control. His interactions and arcs with the half new, half old cast of characters feel genuine. The story of the dark ones and how it ties in with our Ranger's is handled neatly too. While 2033 showed us the desperation of the world, this game shows us a more hopeful side. There are a few questionable things and some plot device moments, but this is forgivable given that it does service the game well and never compromises the structure. I did encounter a few technical hitches. The game sometimes goes into a black screen between chapters and there is the rare glitch on the surface sections, which is probably due to the fact that the game wasn't designed for a exploration oriented experience. But none of these things are gamebreaking and it actually runs pretty well for the way it looks. TLDR: So to sum it up, it is more of the same from 2033, plus some more. The plot isn't a grand sequel and is pretty much a continuation, but it resolves satisfyingly some of the recurring elements while also introducing its own. You likely bought this as a bundle with the first game, and even if you found yourself unpleasantly dragging through that, I'm willing to bet that you'll be pleasantly surprised by the end of Last Light. The Metro games, for me don't stand for a central theme or concept. They're not reflections of the human condition or anything like that. What they are, is a great shooting/stealth experience with a decent challenge, believable world and investable characters. But if you want them to be any of the former, they sure are strong enough for that. 7.5/10

title: metro: last light redux
text: This game is great! And a ton of fun!...but not worth full price. The game game has a lot of mechanic related improvements over 2033 Redux and is a lot less buggy. It also has a longer campaion, but it just doesn't deliver as good of a quality of story as the first one does, nore does it really seem to care about your actions like the first. Let me ewxplain: 1+) Mechanics - Like 2033 Redux, Last Light Redux uses the same HUD display that can be removed based on the style you choose to play on, and no real changes have been made to that. The real improvements have come in the stealth system wich is noticalby more advanced (or at least more sensative) and which does a better job of really kepping you on your toes as you play. Its honestly a nice improvement. 2+)Buggs - While this game is by no means perfect, a lot of the buggs from the first are no longer an issue. Don'e get me wrong, there are bugs, and if you look at the community forum you'll see about 10k ways to fix them all, but its better than 2033 Redux. 3+/-) The campaion - In last light the campaion is much longer than in 2033 (about 2x) and there is another probably 0.5x in bonus material added on as well in the main menue. That said, the campaion gets a bit flat about half way through and at some point starts dragging along. It's still good (a lot better than some big tittles out there) but it just isn't as good as the first and that's kinda a let down coming from playing 2033 Redux. 4-) The Moral Point System - Alright, I'll be honest, this system was annoying in 2033 Redux as well, but the issue here is that the longer campaion means there is more of these points to look out for and more ways to screw them up. It also doesn't seem to matter too much at the end as there is still almost the exact same play sequence regardless of ending, just a different 20sec clip plays after it. Also, while talking about this, the ending doesn't care how you played. Regardless of if you went sneaking or if you went guns blazing, you get the same fight sequence (event for both endings) and while it is crucial to the plot...it just seems sorta cheap. The game reards you the whole time for playing a certian way, and then doesn't really care at the end. It just takes some of the fun out of it. Final thoughts on this game are that one should try to get it when its on sale or part of a combo with 2033 Redux. Its not bad, but I don't really feel its worth the full price they charge for it.

title: metro: last light redux
text: I enjoyed it but my biggest gripe with this game and a lot of games today is the morality system. Metro Last Light probably has the single worst morality system I have ever seen in +1k hours of gaming. What is the point of designing and implementing so many various post-apocalyptic style guns and improvised weapons if the game penalizes you for using them? Now granted, you can throw caution to the wind and kill every single ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you come across with your bloodlust and accept the "Bad/Evil ending" as your penance for the brutal, anarchaic, warmongering, murdering ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you are... But that ending is♥♥♥♥♥♥ A breath taking and death defying adventure with danger at every corner coupled with the anxiety over your dwindling supplies as you trudge through the darkest of Moscow's subway system brutally cut off at the end. And there is absolutely no forgiveness. It's completely all or nothing. Yes, you can spend 11 hours tediously sneaking up behind every guard, spare everyone's life, give every bit of your money to the poor, kiss babies, and volunteer at the soup kitchen every wednesday of the month, But then you get that one lapdance. Suddenly, you're the antichrist himself. Okay, I exaggerate. Still there's no indication how far to one side you're leaning. You maybe be shooting for the good ending, and suddenly get surprised with the bad ending. The decision ultimately feels arbitrary, and it comes off like the game only wants you to play it a certain way. No, I don't want that in my games. The morality system soured the whole experience. An ending is supposed to leave you wanting more, but this has left me wanting to go play something else. I give it a 5/10. However, if I played through the game and Alt F4'd out of the final scene to go watch the ending I want on youtube, I would give it an 8/10. Or better yet do away with the morality system altogether and I would give it an 8/10. This game could have been massively improved with one awesome ending as the grand finale. The game was gorgeous and a lot of love was put into the story, but it's merits were over shaddowed by the morality system. TL;DR watch the ending on youtube.

title: mini ninjas
text: Mini Ninjas is a great game if you like simple exploration games that pose little challenge. However, it has flaws. I recommend Mini Ninjas to anyone who enjoys Zelda games or basic action games. The idea in Mini Ninjas is that you are a the final ninja in a town who is sent to do two things: rescue 5 other lost ninjas and defeat the evil samurai that has brought evil to the land. The villain has turned many of the forest animals into evil samurais; these samurais serve as your primary enemies in this game. For the vast majority of the game, you will be running and fighting through fairly open exploration levels. I say "fairly" open level because while they give the initial appearance of being quite large, this is pretty much an illusion. The levels are mostly quite linear and I do not believe I ever was lost about where to go. While that is nice, I do wish the game relied on a more typical Zelda-style open world instead of using actual levels. Yes, this game actually runs you through levels, with the primary purpose of the levels being to limit you to the current area/region you are in. Because of this, you only have one way to go back and collect the items you missed. Replay the level. This is not a good feature of this game because it comes with several kinds of items to collect(statues, freeing animals, finding plants to use, etc.). I enjoy finding items. I do not enjoy having to replay 45 minutes of gameplay because I missed one item. I will also add that you get absolutely nothing for collecting all of an item on a level. If you find every single Jizo Statue(one of the itesm) on a level, you get nothing. Zippo. Odd. One of the really neat ideas in this game is that you are a ninja who possesses a few unique  ninja powers. You can use stealth to sneak up on enemies and sneak-kill them or you can use a variety of spells to attack. You can even use ninja items like smoke bombs and shurikens to either distract or damage them. However, these unique ninja skills end up exposing a major design flaw in the game. If you don't kill the enemies, you do not get their experience, which you need to upgrade your character and grow stronger and more resilient. The game should have rewarded the player for being a sneaky ninja. It doesn't. Additionally, as you rescue your fellow ninjas, you get to swap between them and use their powers. Unfortunately, their powers are almost entirely useless and none of them can use magic. Therefore, despite rescuing 5 ninjas throughout the game you end up relying on your initial ninja for 95% of the game. 2 of the new ninjas we rescued remained entirely unused because they offered nothing to help me through the game. Disappointing. Well, I've gone and listed some major flaws in the game, yet I am still recommending it. Why? It's actually quite a bit of fun and actually plays like a first game in what would have eventually become a great series. All the flaws I've listed above could have been repaired in the sequels. Despite having weaknesses, I had a blast playing through most of this game. It helps greatly that this is the easiest game I've played in many years. Sometimes you want a challenge, but in a game like this, it actually helped that it was easy. It was very much a game that kids could play; even when you kill enemies in this game, they return to animal form instead of dying. I had a grin on my face a lot of times while playing this game because it has a great sense of whimsy, wonderful art direction, lovely music, and smooth enough gameplay. Despite critiquing it, it was a lot of fun. Let me end by focusing entirely on the positive. While majorly flawed, the game saves itself with its incredible charm and bubbly personality. Combine that with little to no challenge and you have a lovely family-friendly game. I still enjoyed collecting items despite there being no purpose and I even liked fighting the enemies even though there was little skill involved. The game took me 11 hours to beat, though You could reduce that time by 25% if you don't bother to run around and take it all in. This game provided a very nice experience and was well worth the 11 hours I put into it. Had the game been a 25+ hour game, it would have severely hurt its rating, but for a pretty short game, it was nice. I will add one final minor beef, though. Where are the Steam Achievements? The game had a achievements on the Xbox 360 and PS3. Why were those not copied over to Steam? My final rating of the game: 6/10 - Nice, but flawed. I wish there had been sequels that repaired some of the issues.

text: This game is a gem. Back when it was the nintendo DS era I picked up a this game called "Mini Ninjas" I loved the hell out of it. Now, 8 years later I go on a nostalgic trip and rediscover this game on steam. I fell in love with it all over again. Pros: -Large open world levels of lush and beautiful settings of dynasty era Japan -Has replayability with all the hidden or non hidden objectives in each level which you need to get if you want to ace the level -Clean/easy on the eye artsytle that compliments the setting of the worlds perfectly -Multiple characters to choose from, you can choose out of 6 characters which you unlock as you play all with their own weapons and specials -Many different ways to aproach each level. You have a choice of fighting with magic (Kuiji), fighting head on with just your sword (depends on which character you pick), Or you can just not fight at all and stealth your way through the level. The stealth component involves you climbing rooftops and landscapes, hiding between bushes and snow piles, using smoke bombs and special camo magic, and timing your way out of enemy vision -Relaxing and just good fun Cons: - Camera angle. for the most part the camera angle is good and balanced but then there are always some parts of the levels that really mess up the camera specially in tight spaced parkour areas. - You can only play as Hiro (main protaginist) when facing the bosses in boss levels. - some levels leave you with no option but to fight and dont allow stealth. - The swimming and sailing on boat can be very frustrating. Swimming is a slow painful process and when on your boat you can easily lose control and just crash into everything. - The combat is very simple and provides no challenge unless you are facing the ninja minions or the mage minions Overall Mini Ninjas is a beautiful and simple stealth and combat inspired game set in a lush Japanese dynasty era that provides you with a relaxing yet still action filled gameplay experience. 9/10
